why: The student says the local variable c gets the value 0 just by being declared. That is the 'local variables get a default value' misconception: in Java, c has no value yet, so println(c + 1) does not compile.

concepts.quote: int c; declares c, so c is 0.
concepts.why: A local declared without a value stays unassigned, and reading it before an assignment is a compile error, not 0.
This breaks the rule that a variable must be assigned before it is read. None of the variable L0 ways fits exactly, so the closest is used.
The answer makes no claim about int range or int arithmetic.
The answer makes no claim about primitive types themselves.
The answer does not mention double.
